lesson.title: Writing the Blueprint: Class Definition, __init__, and self
lesson.summary: Defining a class means writing methods inside its body, including the special __init__ method that sets up every new object's starting attributes, with self as the name each method uses to refer to the specific object it was called on.
lesson.body:
The earlier examples defined classes with nothing but pass, and then attached attributes to objects from outside, one line at a time. Real classes define their structure up front, inside the class body itself, using methods: functions written inside a class that operate on objects built from that class. The most important method is __init__, which Python calls automatically every time a new object is created, making it the natural place to set up whatever data that object should start with.

```python
class Dog:
    def __init__(self, name, breed):
        self.name = name
        self.breed = breed

    def bark(self):
        return f"{self.name} says Woof!"

rex = Dog("Rex", "Labrador")
print(rex.bark())
print(rex.name, rex.breed)
```

```
Rex says Woof!
Rex Labrador
```

Every method defined inside a class, including __init__, takes self as its first parameter. self refers to the specific object the method is being called on, which is how bark knows to use "Rex" rather than some other dog's name: when you call rex.bark(), Python automatically passes rex in as self, exactly as if you had written Dog.bark(rex) yourself. Inside __init__, the lines self.name = name and self.breed = breed take the values passed in as arguments and attach them to that particular object, so from then on rex.name and rex.breed hold onto them.

It helps to notice that __init__ never has to return anything, and never explicitly returns the new object either; Python handles creating the object and returning it as part of the instantiation process described next. The class body you write here, with __init__ and bark defined inside it, is what the term class definition refers to: the actual code that specifies what every object of this class will be able to do and what it will start out knowing about itself.
